metadata.title: Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm, entropy compression method and the subset gas
metadata.authors: Paula M. S. Fialho, Bernardo N. B. de Lima, Aldo Procacci

nodes.name: Dependency graph
nodes.statement: A graph $\GG$ with vertex set $\FF$ such that each event $\ev\in \FF$ is independent of the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\FF \setminus \Gamma^*_\GG(\ev)$, where $\Gamma^*_\GG(\ev) = \Gamma_\GG(\ev) \cup \{\ev\}$.

nodes.name: Abstract polymer system (APS)
nodes.statement: A triple $(\PP, \mathbf{w}, W)$ where $\PP$ is a countable set of polymers, $\mathbf{w}: \PP \to \mathbb{C}$ assigns activities $w_\gamma$, and $W: \PP \times \PP \to \{0,1\}$ is a symmetric Boltzmann factor with $W(\gamma,\gamma)=0$.

nodes.name: Grand canonical partition function
nodes.statement: $Z_\Lambda(\bm w) = \sum_{S \subset \Lambda,\, S \in I(\GG)} \prod_{\gamma \in S} w_\gamma$, summing over finite independent sets in the support graph $\GG$.

nodes.name: Subset gas
nodes.statement: An APS where $\PP = \{\gamma \subset \VU: |\gamma|<\infty\}$ and $W(\gamma,\gamma')=0$ iff $\gamma \cap \gamma' \neq \emptyset$, so polymers carry a cardinality.

nodes.name: Variable setting (Moser-Tardos)
nodes.statement: Probability space $\Omega = \prod_{x\in\Lambda}\Psi_x$ generated by mutually independent variables $\{\psi_x\}_{x\in\Lambda}$; events depending only on $\psi_A$ for $A \subset \Lambda$ are called tempered, with $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)=A$.

nodes.name: Uniform variable setting
nodes.statement: Variable setting where all $\psi_x$ take values in a common space $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$ uniformly. Determined by the pair $(\Lambda, k)$.

nodes.name: Seed and tidy event (uniform setting)
nodes.statement: A non-empty $X \subset \mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ is a seed of $\ev$ if $\ev|_X = [k]^X$ and $|\ev|=k^{|X|}$. An event is tidy if elementary, or for all $y\in \mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ there exists a seed $X \subset \mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus\{y\}$.

nodes.name: Power of an event
nodes.statement: $\|\ev\| = |\mathrm{supp}(\ev)| - \kappa(\ev)$, where $\kappa(\ev)$ is the common seed cardinality of a tidy event (and $\kappa(\ev)=0$ if elementary).

nodes.name: Seed (general variable setting)
nodes.statement: A proper subset $U \varsubsetneq \mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ such that, given $\omega$ with $\ev$ occurring, resampling $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus U$ leaves every $\ev'\in \FF$ with probability at most $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev')$, and no $U'\supset U$ has this property. An event is tidy if all its seeds have the same nonzero cardinality $\kappa(\ev)$ and for every $x\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ some seed avoids $x$.

nodes.name: Power (general)
nodes.statement: $\|\ev\| = |\mathrm{supp}(\ev)| - \kappa(\ev)$ if $\ev$ is tidy, otherwise $\|\ev\| = |\mathrm{supp}(\ev)|$.

nodes.name: Witness forest
nodes.statement: Forest $F$ obtained from the algorithm record $\mathcal{L}$ by adding isolated vertices for atoms in $\Lambda \setminus X_{F'}$ with label $(x,\emptyset)$ and padding each internal vertex $v$ with label $(x,\ev)$ to have exactly $\|\ev\|$ children using leaves $(y,\emptyset)$.

nodes.name: Admissible sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence $S=\{(x_1,\ev_1),\dots,(x_n,\ev_n)\}$ such that $x_i \in \mathrm{supp}(\ev_i)$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev) \leq \mu_\ev / \prod_{\ev'\in \Gamma^*_\GG(\ev)}(1+\mu_{\ev'})$ for each $\ev\in\FF$, then $\mathrm{Prob}\big(\bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev\big) > 0$.
assumptions: $\FF$ is a finite family of events in a probability space $\Omega$
$\bm{\mu}=\{\mu_\ev\}_{\ev\in\FF}$ is a collection of nonnegative numbers

nodes.name: Fernandez-Procacci criterion
nodes.statement: If $|w_\gamma| \leq \mu_\gamma / \Xi_\gamma(\bm\mu,\GG)$ with $\Xi_\gamma(\bm\mu,\GG)=\sum_{S\subseteq\Gamma^*_\GG(\gamma),\,S\in I(\GG)}\prod_{\gamma'\in S}\mu_{\gamma'}$, then $Z_\Lambda(\mathbf{w})\neq 0$ for all finite $\Lambda\subset\PP$.

nodes.name: Cluster Expansion Local Lemma (CELL)
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev) \leq \mu_\ev / \Xi_\ev(\bm\mu,\GG)$ with $\Xi_\ev(\bm\mu,\GG)=\sum_{S\subseteq\Gamma^*_\GG(\ev),\,S\in I(\GG)}\prod_{\ev'\in S}\mu_{\ev'}$, then $\mathrm{Prob}\big(\bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev\big) > 0$.

nodes.name: Pegden's algorithmic LLL extension
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev) \leq \mu_\ev/\Xi_\ev(\bm\mu,\GG)$ in the variable setting with tempered events, then $\mathrm{Prob}\big(\bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev\big) > 0$ and \textsc{Resampling} terminates in expected $\leq \sum_{\ev}\mu_\ev$ steps.
assumptions: $\Lambda$ finite with associated mutually independent variables $\psi_\Lambda$
$\FF$ is a family of tempered bad events with natural dependency graph $\GG$
conclusions: \textsc{Resampling} finds $\omega \in \bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev$ in expected number of steps $\leq \sum_{\ev\in\FF}\mu_\ev$

nodes.name: Entropy compression lemma
nodes.statement: In the uniform variable setting with tempered tidy flaws, if there is $\alpha>0$ with $(1+\sum_{s\in E'_\FF} d_s\alpha^s)/\alpha < k$, then $\bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev \neq \emptyset$ and \textsc{entropy compression} finds such a configuration in expected steps linear in $|\Lambda|$.
assumptions: Pair $(\Lambda, k)$ given with family $\FF$ of tempered tidy flaws
There exists $\alpha>0$ such that $(1+\sum_{s\in E'_\FF}d_s\alpha^s)/\alpha < k$
conclusions: \textsc{entropy compression} finds $\omega \in \bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev$ in expected number of steps linear in $|\Lambda|$

nodes.name: Main theorem (Forest-Algorithm criterion)
nodes.statement: If $\min_{\xi>0} \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi < 1$ where $\phi_\FF(\xi)=\sum_{s\in E'_\FF} p_s d_s (\xi+1)^s$, then $\bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev \neq \emptyset$ and \textsc{Forest-Algorithm} terminates in expected number of steps polynomial in $m=|\Lambda|$.
assumptions: $\Lambda$ finite, $\psi_\Lambda$ family of mutually independent random variables
$\FF$ is a family of tempered events depending on $\psi_\Lambda$
conclusions: There exists an evaluation $\omega$ of $\psi_\Lambda$ such that no event in $\FF$ occurs
\textsc{Forest-Algorithm} finds $\omega \in \bigcap_{\ev\in\FF}\bar\ev$ in expected number of steps polynomial in $m=|\Lambda|$

nodes.name: Global subset gas condition
nodes.statement: If there is $a>0$ with $\sup_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{\ev\in\FF,\, x\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev)} \mathrm{Prob}(\ev) e^{a|\mathrm{supp}(\ev)|} \leq e^a-1$, then $\mathrm{Prob}\big(\bigcap\bar\ev\big)>0$ and \textsc{Resampling} terminates in expected $\leq \sum_\ev \mathrm{Prob}(\ev) e^{a|\mathrm{supp}(\ev)|}$ steps.
conclusions: \textsc{Resampling} finds $\omega$ in expected number of steps $\leq \sum_{\ev\in\FF}\mathrm{Prob}(\ev)e^{a|\mathrm{supp}(\ev)|}$

nodes.name: Goodness preservation in Resample
nodes.statement: Consider any call of \textsc{Resample}$(x,\ev)$ and let $Y$ be the set of good atoms at the start. If the call finishes, then all atoms in $Y \cup (\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus S_x(\ev))$ are good.
assumptions: $Y$ is the set of all good atoms at the beginning of the call
conclusions: All atoms in $Y \cup (\mathrm{supp}(\ev) \setminus S_x(\ev))$ are good after the call

nodes.name: Bound on number of phases
nodes.statement: \textsc{Forest-Algorithm} performs at most $m=|\Lambda|$ phases.
conclusions: The number of phases of \textsc{Forest-Algorithm} is at most $m = |\Lambda|$

nodes.name: Witness tree structural properties
nodes.statement: For each tree $\tau' \in F'$ with vertices $v_i,v_j$ labeled $(x_i,\ev_i),(x_j,\ev_j)$: (a) if $v_i$ is a child of $v_j$ then $x_i\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev_j)\setminus S_{x_j}(\ev_j)$; (b) if siblings then $x_i\neq x_j$; (c) any vertex with label $(x,\ev)$ has at most $\|\ev\|$ children.
assumptions: $\tau' \in F'$ is a tree from the forest $F'$ produced by \textsc{Forest-Algorithm}
$v_i, v_j$ are vertices in $\tau'$ with labels $(x_i,\ev_i)$ and $(x_j,\ev_j)$
conclusions: (a) If $v_i$ is a child of $v_j$, then $x_i \in \mathrm{supp}(\ev_j)\setminus S_{x_j}(\ev_j)$
(b) If $v_i$ and $v_j$ are siblings, then $x_i \neq x_j$
(c) Any vertex with label $(x,\ev)$ has at most $\|\ev\|$ children

nodes.name: S-Check probability bound
nodes.statement: For an admissible sequence $S=\{(x_1,\ev_1),\dots,(x_n,\ev_n)\}$, $\mathrm{Prob}(\textsc{S-Check}\text{ with input }S\text{ passes}) \leq \prod_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Prob}(\ev_i)$.

nodes.name: Witness forest probability bound
nodes.statement: For a witness forest $F\in\mathcal{F}_n$ with internal-vertex labels $S_F=\{(x_1,\ev_1),\dots,(x_n,\ev_n)\}$, $\mathrm{Prob}(\textsc{Forest-Algorithm}\text{ produces }F) \leq \prod_{i=1}^{n}\mathrm{Prob}(\ev_i)$.
assumptions: $F \in \mathcal{F}_n$ is a witness forest with $n$ internal vertices

nodes.name: Resampling (Moser-Tardos)
nodes.statement: Iterative algorithm that samples $\omega_0 \in \Psi_\Lambda$ and repeatedly resamples variables in $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ for occurring bad events $\ev \in \FF$ until no bad event holds.
input: Family of mutually independent random variables $\{\psi_x\}_{x\in\Lambda}$
output: An evaluation $\omega \in \Psi_\Lambda$ such that no event of $\FF$ occurs

nodes.name: Entropy compression algorithm
nodes.statement: Backtracking algorithm with input $V_t \in [k]^t$ that builds a partial coloring step-by-step, discoloring $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus G(\ev,y)$ when a flaw $\ev$ appears.

nodes.name: Forest-Algorithm
nodes.statement: Variant of Moser-Tardos: samples $\psi_\Lambda$ once, then while a bad atom $x$ exists, calls \textsc{Resample}$(x,\ev)$ for the smallest pair $(x,\ev)$, recursively resampling $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus S_x(\ev)$ (preserving the seed).
input: Family $\{\psi_x\}_{x\in\Lambda}$ of mutually independent random variables
Totally ordered family $\FF$ of tempered events with seed-rule $S_x(\ev)$ fixed for each $(x,\ev)$

nodes.name: S-Check (validation algorithm)
nodes.statement: Validation procedure that, given an admissible sequence $S$, samples $\psi_\Lambda$ and for $i=1,\dots,n$ checks whether $\ev_i$ occurs (returning failure if not) and otherwise resamples $\psi_{\mathrm{supp}(\ev_i)\setminus S_{x_i}(\ev_i)}$.
output: Verdict: \textit{passes} (all events occurred at their step) or \textit{failure}

nodes.name: Nonrepetitive vertex coloring of a graph
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 2.1 to the family of events $\ev_p$ ($p$ a path of $G$ with $2n$ vertices, repetitively colored). With $d_s \leq s\Delta^{2s-1}$ and $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev_p)=k^{-n}$, the criterion gives $\pi(G) \leq (1+b_0(\Delta))\Delta^2$.

nodes.name: Facial Thue choice index of planar graphs
nodes.statement: For a planar graph $G$ with edge lists of size $k$, applying Theorem 2.1 with $d_s \leq 4s$ and $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev_p)\leq k^{-n}$ for facial paths $p$ of length $2n$ yields $\pi'_{fl}(G)\leq 12$.

nodes.name: Beta-frugal coloring
nodes.statement: For events $\ev_e$ (edge monochromatic) and $\ev_\sigma$ ($\beta$-star monochromatic), Theorem 2.1 with $d_1=\Delta$, $d_\beta\leq \Delta^{1+\beta}/\beta!$ recovers $\chi_\beta(G)\leq \Delta^{1+1/\beta}\beta(\beta-1)^{1/\beta-1}/(\beta!)^{1/\beta}+\Delta$.

nodes.name: Clique upper bound on Xi
nodes.statement: $\Xi_\ev(\bm\mu,\GG) \leq \Xi^{\mathrm{clique}}_\ev(\bm\mu,\GG) \equiv \prod_{y\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev)} \big[1 + \sum_{\ev'\in\FF(y)}\mu_{\ev'}\big]$.

nodes.name: Generating function equation
nodes.statement: $W(z) = z\,\phi_\FF(W(z))$, where $W(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1} Q_n z^n$ and $\phi_\FF(\xi)=\sum_{s\in E'_\FF} w_s (1+\xi)^s$.

nodes.name: Coefficient bound rho
nodes.statement: $Q_n \leq \rho^n$ where $\rho = \min_{\xi>0} \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$.

nodes.name: LLL/APS correspondence
nodes.statement: Events in LLL correspond to polymers in APS; dependent events to incompatible polymers; probabilities to absolute values of activities; positivity of $\mathrm{Prob}(\bigcap\bar\ev)$ to $Z_\Lambda(-|\mathbf{w}|)>0$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of theorem teo1 with entropy compression criterion
nodes.statement: In the uniform variable setting, $p_s=1/k^s$, so setting $\alpha=(\xi+1)/k$, condition $\min_\xi \phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi<1$ is exactly the entropy compression criterion $(1+\sum_s d_s\alpha^s)/\alpha < k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP422.2 (goodness preservation)
nodes.statement: Pick $y\in Y$, suppose by contradiction $y$ is bad after the call; identify the last step $t$ where $y$ flipped to bad inside some recursive Resample, and derive contradiction with that recursive call's termination.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP422.3 (phase count)
nodes.statement: Roots of distinct phases have distinct atom labels because Lemma 3.1 forces $x_l \notin \mathrm{supp}(\ev_s)$ for $l<s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP422.4 (witness tree properties)
nodes.statement: (a) is immediate from the construction; (b) follows from Lemma 3.1 applied to siblings between $i$ and $j$; (c) follows from (a) and (b).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP422.5 (S-Check bound)
nodes.statement: By induction on the step $i$: at step $i$ the seed property ensures $\mathrm{Prob}(\ev_i)$ is the upper bound for $\ev_i$ to occur; multiplying gives the product bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP422.6 (forest probability)
nodes.statement: Random choices in \textsc{Forest-Algorithm} producing $F$ also pass \textsc{S-Check}$(S_F)$, so the forest probability is bounded by the S-Check pass probability, then by Lemma LP422.5.

nodes.name: Proof of main theorem TP422.6
nodes.statement: Bound $P_n$ via unlabeled forests: $P_\Phi \leq \prod_v d_{s_v}p_{s_v}$, sum over plane forests using a generating-function recurrence $W(z)=z\phi_\FF(W(z))$, apply analytic-combinatorics bound $Q_n\leq \rho^n$ with $\rho=\min\phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$, and conclude exponential decay implying polynomial expected runtime.

nodes.name: Encode runtime via witness forest
nodes.statement: $P_n = \mathrm{Prob}(|\mathcal{L}|=n)$ equals the probability that the witness forest associated with the record $\mathcal{L}$ has $n$ internal vertices, since $\mathcal{L} \mapsto F$ is an injection.

nodes.name: Bound $P_F$ via S-Check
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP422.6: $\mathrm{Prob}(\textsc{Forest-Algorithm}\text{ produces }F)\leq \prod_i \mathrm{Prob}(\ev_i)$ for each labeled witness forest $F\in\mathcal{F}_n$.

nodes.name: Sum over labeled forests with same shape
nodes.statement: Group labeled forests $F$ by their unlabeled shape $\Phi=f(F)$: $P_\Phi \leq \prod_{v\in\Phi} p_{s_v}\sum_{F:f(F)=\Phi}1 \leq \prod_{v\in\Phi} d_{s_v} p_{s_v}$.

nodes.name: Tree generating-function recurrence
nodes.statement: Decompose plane forests into trees, define $w_s=d_s p_s$ and $Q_n=\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}_n}\omega(\tau)$. Then $Q_n=\sum_{s\in E'_\FF} w_s \sum_{n_1+\dots+n_s=n-1} Q_{n_1}\cdots Q_{n_s}$ with $Q_0=1$.

nodes.name: Functional equation for $W(z)$
nodes.statement: The generating function $W(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1} Q_n z^n$ satisfies $W(z)=z\phi_\FF(W(z))$ with $\phi_\FF(\xi)=\sum_{s\in E'_\FF} w_s(1+\xi)^s$.

nodes.name: Apply analytic-combinatorics bound
nodes.statement: By Flajolet-Sedgewick Prop. IV.5 (or Drmota Thm. 5), $Q_n\leq \rho^n$ where $\rho=\min_{\xi>0}\phi_\FF(\xi)/\xi$.

nodes.name: Bound $P_n$ via convolution
nodes.statement: $P_n \leq \sum_{n_1+\dots+n_m=n} Q_{n_1}\dots Q_{n_m}\leq \rho^n \binom{n+m-1}{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Conclude polynomial expected runtime
nodes.statement: If $\rho<1$, then $\rho^n\binom{n+m-1}{m-1}\leq \rho^{n/2}$ for $n\geq N=\Theta(m\log^2 m / |\ln\rho|)$, giving $T\leq N(N+1)/2 + \sum_{n>N} n\rho^{n/2}$, polynomial in $m$.

nodes.name: Sample all variables
nodes.statement: Sample all variables $\psi_\Lambda$ to produce the initial evaluation.

nodes.name: Main while-loop on bad atoms
nodes.statement: While there is a bad atom, select the pair $(x,\ev)$ where $x$ is the smallest bad atom and $\ev$ is the smallest event with $x\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev)$ that occurs.

nodes.name: Call Resample subroutine
nodes.statement: Invoke \textsc{Resample}$(x,\ev)$, which resamples $\psi_y$ for $y\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus S_x(\ev)$ and recursively calls \textsc{Resample}$(x',\ev')$ on subsequent bad atoms in $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus S_x(\ev)$.

nodes.name: Output evaluation
nodes.statement: Output the current evaluation once no bad atom remains.

nodes.name: Initialize empty coloring
nodes.statement: Step $0$: set $w_0=0$, leaving every $\psi_x$ uncolored.

nodes.name: Color smallest uncolored atom
nodes.statement: If $w_{i-1}^{-1}(0)\neq\emptyset$, let $y$ be the smallest uncolored atom; take entry $s=v_i\in [k]$ and set $w_{i-1}]^s_y$.

nodes.name: Branch on flaw occurrence
nodes.statement: If no flaw occurs in $w_{i-1}]^s_y$, set $\omega_i = w_{i-1}]^s_y$ and continue. If some flaw occurs, select the smallest flaw $\ev$ (which lies in $\FF(y)$) and set $w_i = w_{i-1}]^0_{G^c(\ev,y)}$ (discoloring $\mathrm{supp}(\ev)\setminus G(\ev,y)$).

nodes.name: Termination check
nodes.statement: If $w_{i-1}^{-1}(0)=\emptyset$, stop and discard remaining entries of $V_t$.

nodes.name: Sample all variables
nodes.statement: Sample all variables in $\psi_\Lambda$.

nodes.name: Iterate over admissible pairs
nodes.statement: For $i=1,\dots,n$: if $\ev_i$ does not occur, return failure; otherwise resample $\psi_y$ for $y\in\mathrm{supp}(\ev_i)\setminus S_{x_i}(\ev_i)$.
